provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Mary had a little lamb
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the rhyme with actions.
The pupils should be able to list different pets.

Introduction:
Today we learn about Mary and her lamb.
We have seen pets in our homes.

Content:
Mary had a little lamb.
Its fleece was white as snow.
Everywhere that Mary went.
The lamb was sure to go.

Class activity:
Children will act out the rhyme.
One child is Mary.
Others follow with lamb actions.

Evaluation questions:
What animal followed Mary?
What color was the lamb?
Have you seen a lamb before?

Summary:
We enjoyed learning about Mary and her lamb.

topics.title: Hickory dickory dock
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the rhyme.
The pupils should be able to count the hours.

Introduction:
Today we learn about a mouse and a clock.
We have seen clocks in our classroom.

Content:
Hickory dickory dock.
The mouse ran up the clock.
The clock struck one.
The mouse ran down.

Class activity:
Children will count with the clock.
One child acts as the mouse.
Others make the clock hands.

Evaluation questions:
What time did the clock strike?
What did the mouse do?
Can you show me one finger?

Summary:
We enjoyed counting with the mouse and clock.

topics.title: Row, row, row your boat
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing the rhyme in pairs.
The pupils should be able to perform rowing actions.

Introduction:
Today we learn about rowing a boat.
We have seen boats on the water.

Content:
Row row row your boat.
Gently down the stream.
Merrily merrily merrily merrily.
Life is but a dream.

Class activity:
Children will sit in pairs.
They will pretend to row together.
They will sing as they row.

Evaluation questions:
Where are we rowing to?
What should we do with the boat?
Can you show me rowing?

Summary:
We enjoyed rowing our boats together.

topics.title: London Bridge is falling down
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing the rhyme.
The pupils should be able to play the bridge game.

Introduction:
Today we learn about a famous bridge.
We have walked over bridges in our area.

Content:
London Bridge is falling down.
Falling down falling down.
London Bridge is falling down.
My fair lady.

Class activity:
Children will form a bridge with hands.
Others will walk under the bridge.
The bridge falls when the song ends.

Evaluation questions:
What bridge are we singing about?
What happens in the rhyme?
Can you make a bridge with your hands?

Summary:
We enjoyed playing the bridge game.

topics.title: Ring a ring o roses
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing in a circle.
The pupils should be able to fall down when told.

Introduction:
Today we learn about a circle game.
We have played games in a circle before.

Content:
Ring a ring o roses.
A pocket full of posies.
Atishoo atishoo.
We all fall down.

Class activity:
Children will hold hands and form a circle.
They will walk around singing.
They will fall down when they sneeze.

Evaluation questions:
What do we do when we sneeze?
How do we hold hands?
Can you show me falling down?

Summary:
We enjoyed falling down in the circle.

topics.title: Bingo the dog
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to clap the missing letters.
The pupils should be able to spell BINGO together.

Introduction:
Today we learn about a dog named Bingo.
We have seen dogs in our neighborhood.

Content:
There was a farmer who had a dog.
And Bingo was his name oh.
B-I-N-G-O.
B-I-N-G-O.
B-I-N-G-O.
And Bingo was his name oh.

Class activity:
Children will clap instead of letters.
Teacher will point to missing letters.
They will spell BINGO with claps.

Evaluation questions:
What is the dog's name?
What do we do instead of letters?
Can you spell BINGO?

Summary:
We enjoyed clapping for Bingo.

topics.title: Ten green bottles
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count down from ten.
The pupils should be able to hold up number cards.

Introduction:
Today we learn about counting bottles.
We have counted objects in class before.

Content:
Ten green bottles hanging on the wall.
Ten green bottles hanging on the wall.
And if one green bottle should accidentally fall.
There'll be nine green bottles hanging on the wall.

Class activity:
Children will hold number cards.
They will count down as bottles fall.
They will sit down when their number is called.

Evaluation questions:
How many bottles are there at first?
What happens when a bottle falls?
Can you count to ten?

Summary:
We enjoyed counting down the bottles.

topics.title: Incy wincy spider
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite with finger actions.
The pupils should be able to talk about up and down.

Introduction:
Today we learn about a spider climbing.
We have seen spiders climbing walls.

Content:
Incy wincy spider climbed up the water spout.
Down came the rain and washed the spider out.
Out came the sun and dried up all the rain.
And Incy wincy spider climbed up the spout again.

Class activity:
Children will use fingers to climb.
One finger for the spider.
Other fingers for rain and sun.

Evaluation questions:
What did the spider climb?
What washed the spider out?
Can you show me climbing up?

Summary:
We enjoyed climbing with the spider.

topics.title: Our own class rhyme
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to make a short rhyme.
The pupils should be able to say it together.

Introduction:
Today we create our own class rhyme.
We have learned many rhymes this term.

Content:
We will make a rhyme about our school.
We will include our classroom and teacher.
We will use simple words we know.

Class activity:
Children will suggest words about school.
Teacher will help make sentences.
Everyone will practice saying it.

Evaluation questions:
What is our rhyme about?
Can you say the rhyme?
What words did we use?

Summary:
We enjoyed making our own class rhyme.

topics.title: Rhyme festival
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing all term rhymes.
The pupils should be able to clap for other groups.

Introduction:
Today we celebrate all our rhymes.
We have learned many rhymes this term.

Content:
Each group will choose a rhyme to sing.
They will add actions to their performance.
We will clap for every group.

Class activity:
Children will be divided into groups.
Each group will perform a rhyme.
Others will clap and cheer for them.

Evaluation questions:
Which rhyme did you like most?
Can you name all rhymes we learned?
Did you enjoy the festival?

Summary:
We enjoyed our rhyme festival celebration.
